comments.note: No observations — code is clean and consistent. All dynamic echo sites use $this->esc() covering textarea content, href attributes, link text, warning messages, hidden inputs, and dropdown labels.

summary: Full test suite (95/95) passes; PHPStan level 8 clean.
Confirmed private esc() helper at PageScaffold.php line 43 using htmlspecialchars(ENT_QUOTES, UTF-8).
Confirmed $this->esc() applied to all XSS-critical echo sites: translated text in textarea, name/hash attributes, URLs, file paths, labels, warning badge title.
Non-esc echo sites verified safe: integers (page numbers, line numbers, counts, JSHelper IDs), hardcoded CSS class strings, and internal render methods returning trusted HTML.
Minor: renderText() helper uses bare htmlspecialchars() without ENT_QUOTES — low risk as output only appears in block-level HTML contexts, not attributes. No AC breach.

comments.note: All XSS-critical dynamic echo sites use $this->esc(): translated text in textarea (line 270), textarea name/hash attributes (line 270), URLs (lines 167/205/213/445), labels/source names, file paths (line 330), warning title (line 447). Non-esc echo sites are safe: hardcoded strings ($icon), integers ($line/$number/$labelID/countWarnings()/$untranslated), and internal HTML render methods.

Minor: renderText() at line 353 uses bare htmlspecialchars($text) without ENT_QUOTES or charset. Does not escape single/double quotes, which could matter in attribute contexts, but renderText() output is only used in /

body contexts, so risk is negligible. Recommend aligning to esc() for consistency.

summary: XSS fix in PageScaffold.php reviewed and approved. esc() helper correctly uses htmlspecialchars(ENT_QUOTES, 'UTF-8'), neutralizing attribute injection and textarea break-out attacks. Applied correctly to all XSS-critical echo sites. renderText() bare htmlspecialchars() at line 353 is acceptable in block-level output context. No blocking issues.
